Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. The discussion with Mr. Rhoades made him aware of the fact that there are more than several concerns with his lease. The Department recommended that he hire an environmental consultant to help him through the cleanup and reporting process of an Act 2 cleanup regarding the discharge of produced fluid and the potential impact of the Reno public water supply. Other violations were discussed regarding the other wells on his lease. Statements that were made by Mr. Rhoades during the meeting:-He is the only owner/operator of Petro Erie Inc-He pumps the wells on the lease himself-One well on the lease is on a timer and pumps when he is not present-Mr. Rhoades does not know what occurred at the site referring to the discharge of produced fluid-Wants the water of the households in Reno tested-Hauled 3 loads of brine, 1 load hauled by Gavin to disposal in OH and 2 loads hauled by Paul Weaver to a frac job in West Virginia-Stated that the tank battery and the impact area was present when he purchased the lease

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/03/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/03/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 946418
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2022
Comments: On March 3, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline, Brooke Millisock, and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of 1,600 barrels of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. The southwest infiltration berm area of excavation has been uncovered and has filled with water. The water from the southwest infiltration berm area is overflowing the excavation depth and is flowing under a tarp. Due to the tarp covering the downgradient area of the excavation, the water overflowing could not be observed and could not be determined to be causing any erosion. The conductivity of the water in the in southwest excavation area was 104 uS/cm. The conductivity of the water in the southwest catch box of the well pad was 374 uS/cm. STL Resources continues to vacuum the water that has been collecting out of the catch boxes on the northwest and southwest corners of the well pad. The conductivity of the water in the northwest catch box was 7,800 uS/cm. Two seeps were observed near the northwest catch box, daylighting out of the slope of the well pad that had been previously excavated. The conductivity of the water in the seeps was 7,200 uS/cm. The water from the seeps is flowing in to an area that has been excavated and is covered by a tarp. The area under the tarp is a low spot in the excavation area the seep water appears to be contained in the low spot. Conductivity screening of the water in the remainder of the northwest infiltration berm excavation area resulted in conductivity less than 200 uS/cm. The DEP recommends collecting water from the seeps and delineating the area under the tarp for excavation of impacted soil. The DEP also recommends investigating where these seeps are originating from and installing corrective measures to eliminate the seeps. In addition to following up with the production fluid spill from January 8, 2022, the DEP did not observe any new erosion at the earthen infiltration berms noticed on February 28, 2022. The DEP did not observe any measures to correct the erosion that occurred. The DEP recommends adding temporary BMPs to these areas to help eliminate further erosion or to fix the earthen infiltration berms that had erosion issues. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EXPAND OPER LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/27/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8272219
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2025 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite (CTS #395411). He stated "there was a hole in containment. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. Approximately 2-3 inches of material had already been excavated and placed into containment onsite. Alderdice, Inc. was onsite removing the material during the inspection. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment. On 04/27/2026 the DEP conducted a follow up inspection. The weather was 52 degrees and sunny. I arrived at 0915 hours. The site appeared stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation onsite. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 188-721 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment. There were several temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment. Recovered material was being removed from the site during the inspection (photo #9). Due to the unknown quantity of the release this has been referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411). The following violations remain open against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1015 hours.

Comments: On 12/27/2024 an Incident Response inspection was conducted the MOR42 Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/27/2024 CNX Resources Representative, Ben Geary, reported an approximately 40-gallon brine release off containment at the MOR42 Well Pad located in East Finley Township, Washington County.CNX Resources representative, Ben Geary, and SPSI representative, Mac Maydak, were on site at time of inspection. Mr. Geary informed the Department that that the release was discovered on Saturday, January 25 at 1:15 pm, that the quantity released was approximately 40 gallons, and that a contractor (SPSI) had been dispatched the same day. Mr. Maydak stated that his crew was dispatched on Saturday (1/25) at approximately 1:40 pm. The origin of the release was stated to be a crack found on a T-joint along a line connecting to a slug catcher to the production tanks, which could be observed in front of the Unit H Gas Processing Unit (GPU).Mr. Geary stated that remediation efforts had taken place Saturday (1/25), Sunday (1/26), and continued into today (1/27). The area remediated at the time of inspection measured approximately 38 by 18 feet and to a depth of 1 inch, excluding the sump created on the western side of the GPU that measured approximately 8 inches in depth. It was made known that field screening was conducted during the remediation efforts with screening values between 2,000 and 12,000 s/cm observed. Mr. Maydak stated that 4 Vac boxes had been filled with removed material at the time of inspection.Mr. Geary stated that the remediation efforts would continue until all conductivity values were below 3,000 s/cm and that the sump would be monitored and any fluid that appears would be screened and removed via vac truck.PA DEP Conductivity probe calibrated on 12/27/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-A crew was on site remediating near the Unit H GPU. A vac truck and vac box were observed near the remediation site (Photos 2-3).-The remediation area near the Unit H GPU and the source of the release were observed. A crack was observed on the T-joint of a line beneath a lock out-tag out tag. The lines appeared to be coated in a white film, obscuring visual observations (Photos 4-6).-The excavated areas located in front of and on the west side of the GPU were observed. It appeared that pad aggregate had been removed down to the larger riprap (Photos 7-8).-Field soil conductivity screening was conducted in various locations of the remediation site. The bottom and side walls of the sump were screened, with conductivity values ranging between1.682 ms/cm(1,682s/cm) and 4.71 ms/cm observed. Screening was conducted along the northern edge of the GPU and values of 2.56 ms/cm and 1.927 ms/cm (1,682s/cm) were observed. An area in front of the adjacent equipment on the western side of the GPU was screened. Values in this area ranged between 2.66 ms/cm and 11.69 ms/cm (Photos 9 -16).Determination:Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release. A violation of 78a64a(a) is being issued for the lack of secondary containment.

Comments: On September 18 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504. The findings were as follows:According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging.The well site was not restored during today's inspection. The site was not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511, 3543627, and 3595504.No E and S Plan was found on site. Although there has been additional growth since the Department's last inspection in July of 2023, lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site.The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.

Comments: On 9/10/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County.This inspection was conducted in response to a referral from OGI Matt Woods (Inspection ID: 4268198 on 9/01/2026; Inspection ID: 4269845 on 9/03/2026). OGI Matt Woods requested that a WQS follow up because of potential surface pollution concerns regarding a plastic-lined pit observed during IR 4269845.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- No equipment related to production and/or well plugging operations was observed on site. The plastic-lined pit documented in IR 4269845 was not observed during this inspection (Photos 11 and 19). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site at the time of inspection. No plugging monument was observed at the former location of the well. The API number and Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) were found on site (Photos 16 and 17).- The access road and well site remain heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. Some mulch and seed was observed on site. However, the mulch and seed implemented on site is inadequate, as large portions of exposed soil are observable (Photos 12-15 and 20-21).- No perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site. No E and S Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the violations issued in IR 4263564 against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site will remain outstanding. An additional violation is being issued in this inspection for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The Department requests that the Operator provide an electronic copy of the Control and Disposal Plan and provide clarification regarding the purpose of the plastic-lined pit observed during the time of IR 4269845, what it contained, and method of disposal used. Please provide this clarification no later than 9/29/2026. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon receipt and review of the clarification from the Operator.

Comments: On 11/17/23 an incident inspection of the Coastal Greene Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 11/17/23. Background:On 11/17/23 Greylock self-reported a brine release on the Coastal Greene Well pad. On 11/17/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 10-15 barrels of impaired water had been released to the pad surface from a failure of the 8MH GPU unit. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the pad area and no water ways were impacted. Mr. Eighmey said that Greylock would have equipment, a containment, and a roll off box on site by 1-2pm on 11/17/23. Findings:-An act 9 sign was present at the entrance to the well site (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from the 8MH GPU units (Photo #2,6).-Standing water and a wet spot was observed around the GPU units (Photos #2,3,5,6,8,9).-Elevated conductivity was observed in standing water around the GPU units (Photo #4,7). -Crews were present on-site working to repair the GPU units. (Photos #2-6). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No impacts to WoC were observed. Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a54, and 78a64(a)b are being issued for the release of brine to the ground and failure to have the GPU units in secondary containment for a well drilled in 2018.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/09/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Keating Twp, McKean county. 78.66(c) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to properly report and describe a reportable release of brine by telephone, including pertinent information on: name, address and telephone number of the company and person reporting the incident, date & time of the incident or when it was detected, location and cause of the incident, quantity of brine released, impacts to soil, groundwater or surface water, and remedial actions.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/09/2022
Violation Code: 78.66(c) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to properly report and describe a reportable release of brine by telephone, including pertinent information on: name, address and telephone number of the company and person reporting the incident, date & time of the incident or when it was detected, location and cause of the incident, quantity of brine released, impacts to soil, groundwater or surface water, and remedial actions.
Violation ID: 964824
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

Comments: On December 3, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4084771 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. Violations were issued in IR 4084771 for the loose sediment observed in the channel that empties into the Sediment Trap, the improperly installed super silt fence, and for failure to have a written restoration plan narrative onsite. Additional violations were issued in IR 4106474 and in IR 4103246 for failure to restore the well site by 10/30/2025, in accordance with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A. The NOV Response(s) to IR 4084771, IR 4106474, and IR 4103246 was requested from the operator by 12/04/2025.The First Modification to the COA was entered on 5/01/2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites." Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign remains installed at the entrance of the access road (photo 1). No site restoration plans were found on site during this inspection. Although site stabilization and progress of restoration could not be completely evaluated during this inspection due to the snow cover, it is still evident through the snow cover that the site has not attained greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth (photos 5, 8, and 9). Comments: On 7/17/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection was conducted in response to notification from Seneca of the installation of a concrete catch basin and corrugated pipe on the north side of the pad to capture surface waters on the pad. It was 70 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. I was unaccompanied during the inspection. When I arrived on site, I observed a trench that had recently been dug along the north side of the pad, the trench leading to a 4' x 2' x 2' deep cement catch basin as seen in pictures 12, 13, and 14. I did observe liquid in the trench that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS5 meter. The upper limit of the meter for conductivity is 19.99 mS. The liquid was flowing into the cement catch basin. A vac truck was staged on site with hose ends located in the catch basin, able to remove the accumulating liquids. The fluids were being transferred to a frac tank that had been staged near the catch basin. I inspected the bottom of the center rock lined outfall on the north side of the pad where it leads into the sediment basin. I did not observe liquids discharging from the pad into the basin during this inspection. Liquid in the sediment basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 9.01 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551266 from the sediment basin near the northeast overflow.13 wells have been completed at the site and were staged for flow-back/production. Sand separators and three-phase separators were installed on each of eight recently completed wellheads. The three-phase separators were being used to separate water, gas, and oil. The rig/frac operations secondary containment structure remains installed around the well heads, the sand separators and the three-phase units. Two produced water tanks and 13 GPUs were stationed in secondary containment. Nine frac tanks have been installed in secondary containment south of the eight new gas wells, these being used for flow-back. 32 frac tanks used during fracking operations remain stationed in secondary containment on the west side of the pad.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1030 hours.

Comments: On November 5, 2025, the DEP conducted a Restoration Inspection of CNX's Herminie Well Site (ESG076523008-00) located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County following a Post-Drilling Site Restoration Report (PDSRR) submission the DEP received on 10/17/2025 (Final well drilled: 129-29261 Drilling Completed on: 1/30/2025.) In accordance with 78a.65, within 9 months after the completion of drilling a well or expiration of the permit for the last well drilled, the Operator shall restore the well site. 9 months after the completion of drilling for the last well drilled at the Herminie Well Site is 10/30/2025. At the time of this inspection the DEP observed the Act 9 sign at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the onsite mailbox, the DEP observed a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan as well as an Emergency Response Plan both with all required components. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an access road that was stabilized with gravel, to the right of the access road entrance, the DEP observed an infiltration basin and outlet. The basin and outlet appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, the outlet was not observed to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and Compost Filter Sock (CFS) was observed to still be installed at the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, a soil stockpile located adjacent to the access road was observed to be exhibiting at least 70% vegetative cover, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the base of the stockpile.At the time of this inspection, a second infiltration basin was observed to be located adjacent to the access road, this basin and its outlet were observed to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, the South Perimeter of the well pad and a soil stockpile located adjacent to the well pad was observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover, however, it was observed to be thoroughly seeded/mulched. A third infiltration basin and outlet was observed adjacent to the well pad on the south perimeter, these features appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, they too were exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover and had CFS installed around the basin and outlet.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the other perimeters of the well pad to be nearing the 70% vegetative cover requirement and CFS was observed to be installed at the edge of the perimeters. Included in the Limit of Disturbance for this site, is a smaller gravel pad. The perimeters of this gravel pad and its access road were observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative growth and were thoroughly seeded and mulched with CFS installed on the perimeter edges. At the time of this inspection, the DEP did not observe any drilling equipment not necessary for production to be located on the well site. Based on today's inspection, it appears the Herminie well site is not meeting the requirements set forth in 78a.65 Site Restoration, therefore the DEP is recommending the PDSRR Submission be denied. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit a PDSRR upon complete restoration of the Herminie well site in accordance with 78a.65.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of the completion of the final well.

The basin and outlet appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, the outlet was not observed to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and Compost Filter Sock (CFS) was observed to still be installed at the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, a soil stockpile located adjacent to the access road was observed to be exhibiting at least 70% vegetative cover, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the base of the stockpile.At the time of this inspection, a second infiltration basin was observed to be located adjacent to the access road, this basin and its outlet were observed to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, CFS was observed to still be installed around the infiltration basin outlet.At the time of this inspection, the South Perimeter of the well pad and a soil stockpile located adjacent to the well pad was observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover, however, it was observed to be thoroughly seeded/mulched. A third infiltration basin and outlet was observed adjacent to the well pad on the south perimeter, these features appeared to be constructed and functioning according to PCSM plans, however, they too were exhibiting less than 70% vegetative cover and had CFS installed around the basin and outlet.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the other perimeters of the well pad to be nearing the 70% vegetative cover requirement and CFS was observed to be installed at the edge of the perimeters. Included in the Limit of Disturbance for this site, is a smaller gravel pad. The perimeters of this gravel pad and its access road were observed to be exhibiting less than 70% vegetative growth and were thoroughly seeded and mulched with CFS installed on the perimeter edges. At the time of this inspection, the DEP did not observe any drilling equipment not necessary for production to be located on the well site. Based on today's inspection, it appears the Herminie well site is not meeting the requirements set forth in 78a.65 Site Restoration, therefore the DEP is recommending the PDSRR Submission be denied. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit a PDSRR upon complete restoration of the Herminie well site in accordance with 78a.65.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of the completion of the final well.

Comments: On August 31 2023, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Adams 877-5 OG Well. The findings were as follows:The well site was located in an open field. The access road appeared stabilized at the time of this inspection. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of this inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. Comments: On 09/07/2026 at ~ 1950 hours a mist was observed coming out of the top of the produced fluid tank at Expand's Deremer Well Pad in Tuscarora Township, Bradford County. On 09/08/2026 at ~ 0830 hours Expand representative Mike Deming contacted me via phone to inform me of the release. At ~ 0846 hours Expand representative Steve Moyer called in the release to the DEP 24 hour hotline. He stated more fluid was discovered more fluid on the ground. It is estimated that ~ 25 gallons of produced fluid was released on and off containment. Creston Environmental will be onsite to scrape up the material. At ~ 0930 hours I arrived onsite to conduct an incident inspection. I met with Mike Deming. The area of the reported release had been delineated. He stated the area of release is ~ 660 square feet (photo #3-5). The cause of the release was due to the dump line being stuck open which was caused by a technical communication malfunction. Fluids in the area of the release were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~ 19.99 mS/cm. Fluids outside the area of released were field measured for EC between 425-800 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. There was a lined dumpster onsite for the scraped material to be placed in (photo #7). Creston Environmental was conducting screening during the inspection. Remedial work did not yet begin while I was onsite. At ~ 1215 hours the DEP received photos of the remediated area (photos #8-10). Based on the reported release the following violations are cited as are immediately corrected against API #015-23796:CLS 402(b)I departed the site at 1000 hours.

Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2/21/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator concerning the discovery of fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC) in the north central area of Pad B. It rained heavily while I was traveling up the access road and it stopped before I reached Pad B. Along the access road, a sediment discharge into UNT 18 to Frozen Run was observed. Sediment-laden fluid was observed flowing from the access road, underneath a section of silt fence, overtop of a line of compost filter sock, and entering the stream. It was noted in inspection report number 3505502 from 2/13/23 that the potential for a sediment discharge continued to exist in this location due to stormwater from the access road overtopping a line of compost filter sock. The Department recommends adding additional compost filter sock to prevent additional sediment discharges into the stream. Violations remain outstanding for the sediment discharge into the UNT 18 to Frozen Run along the access road. These violations remain outstanding against the ESCGP.On Pad B, the pad was covered with puddles of stormwater due to the recent precipitation. In the northcentral area of the pad, an excavated section approximately 60 feet by 10 feet is present along the pad edge where the pad meets the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid in this area was between 17.18 mS/cm and greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A sump is installed in the pad surface to the south of the north stormwater channel. Fluid is present in the sump approximately 2 feet down and an EC reading could not be obtained at this depth. The fluid in the north stormwater channel in the north central area had an EC of 11.97 mS/cm. The fluid flowing out of the northeast end of the north stormwater channel and into the lined sump has an EC ranging between 16.14 mS/cm and 19.18 mS/cm. The fluid within the lined sump at the end of the channel had an EC of 18.05 mS/cm. It appears that all of the fluid flowing out of the stormwater channel at the surface is being collected by the lined sump. No fluid was observed surrounding the sump. EC readings of the soil surrounding the sump were all below 200 uS/cm. In the northwest area of the pad surface where the dancefloor had been located, the stormwater had an EC of approximately 1600 uS/cm or less. The EC of fluid in the stormwater channel at the northwest corner of the pad was approximately 1400 uS/cm. Northwest of the MASS the fluid on the pad surface had an EC of 2.48 mS/cm. In the northeast corner of the pad surface, the EC of the fluid was 5.26 mS/cm. The fluid east of the MASS had an EC of 2.39 mS/cm. The fluid within the secondary containment southeast of the MASS was approximately 8 mS/cm. Fluid near the southeast corner of the pad, where elevated EC fluid was found by the Department on 2/6/23, had an EC of 2.80 to 4.68 mS/cm. The Department recommends screening the entire pad surface for elevated electrical conductivity and vacuuming up any fluid found with elevated electrical conductivity.Violations noted for the fluid discovered in the northcentral area of the pad surface. Due to the unknown volume and origin of this fluid, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation.

Comments: On November 29, 2023, DEP representatives Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted a incident inspection at the Inflection Energy Reynolds Well Pad. Gregg Saunders with Inflection Energy reported on November 28, 2023 that a spill from a separator onsite occurred misting production fluid onto the well pad surface. A valve body on the separator failed and spilled approximately 10 gallons of production fluid onto the well pad surface. Penn E and R was onsite for Inflection and delineated the area of impact. Inflection contractors were using a high vacuum truck to remove some of the impacted area and excavating the remainder of the area where the vacuum truck was not able to handle. Soil conductivity was screened with a soil conductivity meter and ranged from 200 uS/cm to an over range reading on the meter. The upper conductivity limit of the DEP soil conductivity meter is 4,000 uS/cm. The lower range measurement was from an area that the impacted soil had been removed.The spill of production fluid outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management 301.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/22/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8169356
Permit API: 081-21941
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/22/2023
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of approximately 2 barrels of produced fluid. The release occurred on 12/21/23 around 14:30. The release occurred on the northwestern pad corner behind the Comtech units allowing the fluid to flow off the pad toward a compost filter sock berm. A hose came off of one of the Comtech units and sprayed the produced water past the containment and onto the ground.Spoke with Matt Tusing, Penn E and R. The impacted area was cleaned up yesterday. Today, they will continue conductivity screening and collect confirmation samples as required for remediation under Act 2. The impacted area is an irregular shape with sides that are 30 feet, 24 feet, 25 feet, and 27 feet long. The depth of the impacted area is an average of a few inches deep. The removed material filled about 2 rolloff containers and was estimated to be under 125 cubic yards.Conductivity screening was performed by DEP within the impacted area. All results were between 0.34 and 0.58 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). The site was also screened about 50 feet beyond the impacted area. Conductivity readings ranged from 0.01 to 0.21 mS/cm. There were no other visual indicators noted beyond the excavated area.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), 78a56(a), and SWMA 301.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Onsite Follow-up inspection for violations initially issued on 4/7/2017. OGA 3222(B)(3)- failure to submit completion report. 78.122(A) - failure to submit well record. 78.88(E) - failure to submit MIA. 78.121(A) - failure to submit Production. (Conventional) 78.121(B) - failure to submit Production. (Electronically) API # 121-45259. Well has a pump jack with electric motor, 2" tubing w/rods, inside 7" casing, inside conductor casing. Photo #1. 7" casing is open to atmosphere. No venting detected at time of inspection. Photo #2. The well is equipped to produce and is properly labeled with a well tag. Photo #3. There is no Site ID posting onsite. It was observed oil and brine has leaked from the stuffing box and ran between the 7" casing and the open conductor casing. Photo #2. Production reported to the Department for 2023 was 21.43 bbl of oil / 365 days and no gas. MIA reported to the Department for 2023 has 12 psi on primary production string with no corrosion. Corrected violations: 78.88(E) - failure to submit MIA. 78.121(A) - failure to submit Production. (Conventional) 78.121(B) - failure to submit Production. (Electronically) Additional Violations: OGA3211(g).Posting- Operator has failed to post operator information at the well site. 78.73(A). General provision for well construction and operation. Continuing violations: OGA 3222(B)(3)- failure to submit completion report. 78.122(A) - failure to submit well record.
